messages:
Alex: quick heads up — after the midday soak test the elastic reservoir prototype violated tenant headroom in a spillover path. saw two tenants take >2x reserved burst credits and starve smaller tenants :frowning:
Maria: ugh, any repro steps? was this under sustained load or a sudden spike?
Sam: short dump from the operator when it happened:
```
[2026-03-22T15:02:11Z] admit: tenant=alpha credits=5 headroom=1 requested=12 -> admitted
[2026-03-22T15:02:11Z] debit: tenant=alpha burst_used=8
[2026-03-22T15:02:12Z] spillover: allowed=true global_headroom=0.2 -> allocated
[2026-03-22T15:02:13Z] eviction: target=beta preempt_attempts=0 -> failed
```
Alex: looks like the spillover gate allowed allocation even though per-tenant headroom policy should have prevented that. might be a race between admit and debit paths.
Kevin: is this the path where the reservoir drains but the ledger update is async? we ran into similar in the soft-reserve sketch.
Sam: yep — admit does a tentative reserve and returns fast; the debit (final commit) races in from the usage side. if commit fails we don't always revert the tentative in time.
Jordan: tradeoff here: revert-on-failure adds latency and complexity to hot paths. we can tighten admit checks (reject more) or make commit sync (slower). both hit tail latency or utilization.
Maria: can we do a short experiment: keep admit fast but add a short finalizer window (50–100ms) where tentative reservations are flagged and can't be double-spilled? that could catch most races w/o full sync.
Kevin: that sounds reasonable. other option: operator-level conservative cap for tenants with recent high variance (mark them noisy) — they get less spillover. cheap and low-latency.
Alex: agree. propose two parallel mitigations: 1) 100ms finalizer where tentative res is protected from immediate spillover, 2) noisy-tenant cap + probe backoff. then run the sim harness for 24h.
Sam: I'll sketch the config flags:
```
elastic.reservation.finalizer_ms = 100
elastic.noisy_tenant.reduction_pct = 30
elastic.noisy_tenant.window = 120s
```
InfraBot: deploy-trigger: rolling-canary to eng-runtime/stage with tags [elastic-fix-experiment]. CI: green.
Maria: also want an observability delta: histograms for tentative->commit latency and a counter for tentative-timeout-reverts. need those before canary.
Jordan: add a canary group with a synthetic small-tenant mix to validate fairness under spillover.
Kevin: one more thought: document the operator vs control-plane boundary — which side owns admission correctness vs best-effort throughput. I think admit/counters belong control plane, but operator must enforce hard caps.
Alex: yep. I'll write a short follow-up RFC note clarifying: control-plane does fast admits + heuristics; operator enforces hard caps and must never let a tenant exceed hard-reservation. exceptions must be explicit and audited.
Sam: timeline — I'll push the finalizer + metrics PR by EOD, then a stage canary tomorrow morning.
Maria: perfect. @Jordan @Kevin if you both can review the RFC sketch, we can decide whether full sync commit is ever acceptable for premium tenants.
Jordan: will do.
Kevin: same.
Alex: thanks y'all. leaving this open for reviews. :thumbsup:
